solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Queen's protected by God, a symbol of British nationality

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed within it, so the royal letter goes inside the deity's name

parts.note: Dagon was a god of the Philistines
R, for Regina, is the usual abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A patriotic remark: the monarch kept safe under God, an emblem of Britishness.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. Dagon is an Old Testament god; R sits inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: The red dragon on the Welsh flag is a national emblem of Wales, part of Britain.

clue.text: Is married during last month, abandoning the City quarter

indicators.note: during tells us one piece happens within the other
abandoning means dropping letters

parts.note: December is the last month of the year
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone married in late December leaves their district of the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops EC from DECEMBER, leaving D EMBER; 'during' inserts IS M.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarter a body is to cut it into limbs, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Bikini, say, shows most of top everyone's admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: everyone is all; the 's is 'has'

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as a synonym of itself, the word top

explanation.surface: Beachwear in which most of the upper part is on view to all.
explanation.walkthrough: Bikini is a Pacific atoll, not swimwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands is an example of a ring-shaped coral reef.

clue.text: Not a lot of choice of platform at a small station?

definitions.text: choice of platform at a small station?
definitions.meaning: a small station has only two platforms to choose from: the first or the second

explanation.surface: Little option of platforms at a country halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple or so is a small number, and a two-platform station offers just that pair.

clue.text: Incorrect point not obvious to audience

parts.note: off means wrong or mistaken, as in a figure that is off
a stage is a point in a process, as in 'at this stage'

explanation.surface: A complaint that a mistaken point was lost on the listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: What happens out of the spectators' sight, in the wings, is hidden from the people watching a play.

clue.text: Visionary and affecting melody, main part of Rossini opera to which Queen's attached

indicators.note: attached means joined on, so the royal letters follow the rest

parts.note: for can mean concerning or affecting
a tune is a melody

indicators.note: main part of keeps the chief word of the title

parts.note: William Tell is an opera by Rossini
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A moving tune from a Rossini opera with the Queen fixed to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main part of' takes TELL from William Tell.
explanation.definitionFit: A clairvoyant who predicts the future claims to see what is coming.

clue.text: Part of group setting British Standards in animal fat

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat used in cooking
BS is the abbreviation for British Standards

explanation.surface: Part of a group laying down official standards for animal fat.
explanation.definitionFit: In set theory a set contained within a larger set is a portion of that collection.

clue.text: A key southern landmass with no disadvantage, being temperate

parts.note: B is a musical key

indicators.note: with no means take something away

parts.note: a continent is a large landmass
con as in pros and cons is a point against

explanation.surface: A tour of a southern continent with no drawbacks, in a mild climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temperate' suggests climate; here it means restrained in drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone moderate who avoids indulgence, especially in alcohol, refrains.

clue.text: Racecourse record with several failing to finish

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: failing to finish drops the final letter

parts.note: some means several

explanation.surface: A record set at a racetrack when several runners don't finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom, in Surrey, is home to the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey is a famous English horse-racing venue.

clue.text: Reasonable to have affection for a European

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the word for affection stands where the letter a was

parts.note: sane means sensible or reasonable
love is deep affection

explanation.surface: A sensible person is fond of someone from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Slovenia, a country in central Europe, is a European.

clue.text: A shocking line in scene from The Archers?

definitions.text: A shocking line in scene from The Archers?

parts.words: A shocking line in scene from The Archers?
parts.note: a shocking line sounds like a soap's dramatic dialogue, but it is a barrier on a farm that gives a shock

explanation.surface: A dramatic bit of dialogue in a radio soap episode.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap set in a farming village.
explanation.definitionFit: A wired barrier carrying current stops livestock straying on farms like those in the soap.

clue.text: Puzzles concerning public transport

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letter headings
buses are a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Brainteasers about getting around by bus or train.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture puzzles in which symbols and letters stand for words are a kind of word puzzle.

clue.text: Turn to write another hint for solvers missing Celsius for scientist

indicators.note: missing tells us a letter is dropped from what we have so far
turn tells us to read the word for re-hinting backwards

parts.words: to write another hint for solvers
parts.note: to reclue a crossword is to write a fresh clue for it

explanation.surface: A setter's chore: rewriting a clue that lacked the temperature scale, for a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses RECLUE to EULCER; 'missing' drops its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician and physicist.

clue.text: Christian Union in immense high church-wide movement

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other
high means drunk or intoxicated, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: CU is the usual short form of Christian Union, a student society

explanation.surface: A student Christian Union caught up in a huge High Church movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' here means drunk, not the High Church tradition; 'in' sets the union's initials inside the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The movement for unity between the Christian churches spans all denominations.

clue.text: Leader imposing local conditions in speech on instrument

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another is placed after it

parts.note: a bell is a percussion instrument

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: the weather is the state of the atmosphere where you are

explanation.surface: A conductor forcing the weather onto a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: A wether is a castrated ram; the bellwether wore a bell and led the flock.
explanation.definitionFit: The lead sheep of a flock gives its name to anyone who sets a trend others follow.

clue.text: Squire, perhaps, unhappy in a minor way with leader of ramblers

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lane is a minor road
down means dejected

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A country squire, a little glum, joined by the head of the walking club.
explanation.walkthrough: A squire is the chief property-holder in an English village.
explanation.definitionFit: A squire is an example of someone who owns estates or property in the country.

clue.text: Have a look back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for a glance backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: An invitation to take a glance behind you.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain or possess something is to own it, a common synonym pair.

clue.text: Perhaps study doorway has beam built in

indicators.note: built in means inserted inside a structure

parts.note: a portal is a doorway
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A doorway leading to a study with a beam built into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' is not a room but an artist's sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's study is an example of a depiction of a subject.

clue.text: Crush in service area

parts.note: Mass is a church service
an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: A crowd jam in the service station.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat utterly or slaughter is to overwhelm completely.

clue.text: Ruth's head in a thousand curlers seen here?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written
K, from kilo, stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: Ruth, head in a thousand hair curlers, seen at a salon.
explanation.walkthrough: The curlers are players of curling, not hair rollers.
explanation.definitionFit: Curling is played on a sheet of ice, the place where its players are found.

clue.text: Drinks dispenser I wonder about in the coldest months

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: winter is the coldest season of the year

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the pronoun and the word for wonder round

parts.note: awe is wonder or amazement

explanation.surface: A puzzled musing about a drinks machine during the cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the pronoun and wonder round, giving EWAI; 'in' places it inside the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The restaurant employee who serves wine to diners is a sommelier, one who dispenses drinks.

clue.text: Prepared to stuff vegetable in old Spanish dough

indicators.note: to stuff is to fill, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: A recipe for a stuffed vegetable in a Spanish pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: Dough is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The former currency of Spain was money before the euro.

clue.text: Digger's load dumped centrally in Oxshott, redeveloped awfully

indicators.note: centrally tells us to take the middle three letters of each word

explanation.surface: Spoil dumped in the middle of Oxshott, a posh Surrey village, after appalling redevelopment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumped' is a link to the surface; take SHO, VEL and FUL from the three word centres.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount a spade holds is what someone digging carries in one go.

clue.text: Run away for a break

explanation.surface: Fleeing for a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Flee is a slang sense; and a crack in something is a rupture.

clue.text: Society and state spending will be cut by such a one

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A political warning that cuts in spending are coming.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'such a one' refers back: someone by whom spending is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who puts money by rather than spending it reduces outlay.

clue.text: Utter depravity smothers love

indicators.note: smothers means covers or surrounds

parts.note: vice is wickedness, depravity
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Total wickedness stifles affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like the adjective meaning total; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To say or express something is to speak it.

clue.text: Large insect regularly nearing light

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
an ant is an insect

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter

explanation.surface: A big bug drawing close to a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of nearing: ERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable lamp with a protective case is a source of illumination.

clue.text: Make concrete (around a hundred tons) for repair

indicators.note: around tells us the verb goes round the two abbreviations

parts.note: to reify is to make an abstraction concrete
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Builders mixing concrete by the hundred tons for repair work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make concrete' is not mixing cement but the verb REIFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To put right or correct something is to mend it.

clue.text: Indicate danger of reconstructing New Theatre

indicators.note: reconstructing means building again in another order

explanation.surface: Warning of the perils of rebuilding a playhouse called the New Theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace or signal harm ahead is to warn of trouble.

clue.text: Paint the town red, taking in a show

indicators.note: taking in means holding something inside

parts.note: to paint the town red is to revel, celebrate wildly

explanation.surface: Partying hard on a night out, including a visit to a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like a theatre noun; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose or make visible is to display or expose.
